images.caption: A modern reconstruction of Dimetrodon grandis. The integument is based on evidence from Dimetropus and Estemmenosuchus showing it may have had scaleless skin with rectangular scutes on the underside of the belly. The upright posture is also based on the Dimetropus trackways, which shows Dimetrodon and closely related synapsids may have stood with its legs underneath the body rather than sprawling.

images.caption: A color-coded skull diagram of Colobomycter pholeter, mostly based on a diagram published by MacDougall et al. (2017). Dotted lines indicate missing bone. All alveoli contain teeth in this diagram, while the actual animal replaces a few teeth at a time. Not featured in the legend are the septomaxilla (pale orange, inside the nares), the splenial (yellow, at the bottom of the jaw), and the articular (Bright fuschia, same color as the surangular, back of the jaw).

images.caption: A color-coded skull diagram of Orovenator mayorum, mostly based on a skull diagram published by Ford & Benson (2018). A composite of two specimens, primarily the smaller and more complete holotype (OMNH 74606) but also incorporating information from a larger referred partial skull (OMNH 74607). Proportions are mostly based on the holotype, which is generally considered a juvenile. Dotted lines indicate missing bone or areas of poor preservation.
